acceptance.output_evidence: HOW THE CADENCE WAS MEASURED, and the honest answer first: from ONE day's completion evidence across three firms plus the sources' own declared behaviour -- NOT from a multi-day census. What was read: 49financial completion 2026-09-09 while the calendar's expected last trading day was 2026-09-10 (T-1); inflection completion 2026-09-10, the min() across its three api_dims snapshots (T-0 that morning); cottonwood completion 2026-09-09 (T-1). The runner's own business-date walk (expected_last_trading_day -> prev_trading_day until the whole source set is complete) selected 2026-09-09 for 49F and COT and 2026-09-10 for INF. From that: a TRADING-DAY cadence is the right SHAPE (a calendar-day cadence fires twice a week into a closed market) and MAX_AGE_TRADING_DAYS = 2 -- one missed fire tolerated, two not -- because 1 behind IS the steady state. WHAT THAT MEASUREMENT CANNOT SUPPORT, stated rather than left for the reader to infer: (1) n = 1 DAY, 3 firms; a proper cadence claim wants a completion-date series over weeks, and a source that silently completes T-2 once a month would not appear in this evidence at all; (2) the 09:00 ET TIME is the BRIEF'S, not a measurement -- nothing here establishes that all three sources have completed by 09:00, only that they had completed by the time the runner was invoked, so if a source regularly completes at 10:00 ET every fire would produce a correct but needlessly day-old directory and the system would look healthy while being a day slow; (3) the ceiling of 2 is a DECLARATION on one day's shape, mitigated only by living in ONE place (expiry.py) behind a test. || WHAT THE CONTROLLED CLOCK CANNOT SHOW, by subtraction from what a real scheduled execution involves: TIME ZONES -- the schedule is applied cron(0 9 ? * MON-FRI *) with ScheduleExpressionTimezone America/New_York, read live in arm (g), but the harness never converts a zone, so a WRONG zone would pass every arm; DST -- the zone pin exists precisely so the fire does not walk an hour in March and November, and NO ARM EXERCISES A DST BOUNDARY because that boundary is a property of the SCHEDULER's interpretation, not of this cell's date arithmetic; A MISSED FIRE NOBODY OBSERVES -- the harness shows the DETECTION given a manifest gap, but not that the detection ever RUNS; if the scheduler itself stops firing, no manifest is written and nothing observes the absence, because THE DETECTOR IS INSIDE THE THING THAT FAILED. This cell builds no monitor (standing moratorium), so the honest statement is that a TOTAL SCHEDULER OUTAGE IS INVISIBLE TO THIS SYSTEM BY DESIGN and the first observer is a human or the over-age answer an advisor receives; RETRIES -- the applied target carries MaximumRetryAttempts 185 and MaximumEventAgeInSeconds 86400, and the manifest write is keyed by business date so a retry is idempotent, but that is REASONED, not exercised; CONCURRENCY -- two fires overlapping, or a fire overlapping a read; THE LAMBDA ACTUALLY RUNNING -- arm (g) proves the function exists and carries the built bytes, but NO ARM INVOKES IT and the first real execution is the first scheduled fire; IAM AT RUNTIME -- whether irpt-directory-refresh-role can actually GetObject the directory and PutObject the manifest is DESIRED-plane verified only. THE SHARPEST: the missed-fire detector lives inside the process whose absence it is meant to detect -- it catches a SKIPPED fire and is blind to a STOPPED schedule. || THREE THINGS FOR THE CVO TO CHALLENGE: (1) ENABLED is this project's first live schedule, justified because no vendor client is in the function's import closure; if the bound is read more broadly the one-line change is state = DISABLED; (2) the function does freshness ACCOUNTING and does not BUILD -- build_dispatch: NOT_WIRED is recorded honestly, but a reader skimming 'the refresh schedule is live' could conclude the directory now refreshes itself, and IT DOES NOT until row W1-S8 clears; (3) three id spellings are now in play (rows W2-S9, W1-S7, W2-S11) and each was found only where two cells JOIN.
